subject: Follow-up: Aurora AI competitive trial scope & bake-off success criteria
body:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@aurora.ai>, Priya Nambiar <priya@aurora.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Aurora AI competitive trial scope & bake-off success criteria

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap + proposed concrete next steps so we’re aligned on scope for the competitive trial: we heard Aurora wants a head-to-head validation against your incumbent hyperscaler and one other inference API with emphasis on latency tail, cost per 1M tokens, and end-to-end integration effort.

Proposed bake-off scope (summary):
- Objectives: compare latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec at target qps), model fidelity on 3 evaluation suites, and unit economics (cost per 1M tokens + infra delta).
- Competitors: Aurora incumbent (CloudGiant AI endpoint) + one open inference API per your pick.
- Datasets & tests:
  - Conversational summarization (12K tokens aggregate)
  - Domain Q&A (support logs, 8K tokens)
  - Reranking/long-context extraction (5K tokens)
- Environments: Hosted Redwood API + Redwood Private (VPC) if you want to mirror production networking.
- Success criteria (pass/fail and graded):
  1) p95 latency within 1.5x of CloudGiant at your target qps OR demonstrable graceful degradation under load.
  2) Equivalent or better fidelity on blinded eval sets (Delta F1 <= 2 pts).
  3) 20–40% unit-cost improvement at expected 100k daily tokens OR clear plan to get there via batching/quantization.
- Timeline: smoke test (week of Aug 31), full run (week of Sep 7–11), results review week of Sep 14.
- Deliverables from Redwood: test harness + runbook, baseline matrix, raw logs (latency/cost), and short exec summary.

Attachments: initial Redwood vs hyperscaler comparison matrix (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx) and our proposed MOP (aurora-bakeoff-mop.pdf).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the two competitors you want in the run (your incumbent + fallback)?
2) Share sample prompts / one representative conversation per test suite and an expected QPS target for the test windows.
3) Confirm whether you want Redwood Private (VPC) included for the smoke test or just hosted API.

I’ve looped in Rishi (pricing/contract), Marcus (runtime/test infra), and Marissa (CS + evaluation harness) to own next steps on our side.

If that looks good, we’ll lock the smoke test slot for Aug 31 and circulate access details.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

---

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@aurora.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priya Nambiar <priya@aurora.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:02:14 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Aurora AI competitive trial scope & bake-off success criteria

Thanks Laura — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifications:

- Competitors: yes, keep our current CloudGiant AI endpoint + please add HyperScale ML as the second baseline.
- QPS target: start with 50 qps sustained for the throughput run, then a stress stage to 150 qps to observe tail behavior.
- Data: I’ll share 3 sample conversations per test suite by EOD Monday (Aug 24).
- Private deployment: For the smoke test, please run against Hosted API only. If the smoke looks good, we’ll move to a VPC run in the full week.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood can record per-request memory usage or KV-cache stats? CloudGiant’s numbers hide some of that so we want parity in telemetry.

Thanks — Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, Aurora AI
sanjay.rao@aurora.ai | +1 (650) 555-9922

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Aurora AI competitive trial scope & bake-off success criteria

Team — forwarding the customer confirmation and asks. Action items below (owners + ETA):

- Rishi: prepare a two-tier pricing quote for the trial (hosted trial pricing + estimate for VPC run). Also draft a short contract addendum for trial data retention and logging. ETA: Aug 28.
- Marcus: own test infra + instrumentation. Need to confirm we can surface KV cache stats, GC/mem footprints, and token-level latency breakdowns. Also prepare run commands for spin-up of 50qps and stress to 150qps. ETA: Aug 28.
- Marissa: own evaluation harness and run coordination. Capture the blinded scoring process and tie fidelity metrics to the deliverable report. Coordinate with Aurora for sample files. ETA: Aug 27.

I’ll respond to Sanjay and Priya confirming timeline and ask them to drop the sample prompts (they said EOD Monday). I’ll also attach the draft MOP and the matrix so you have context.

Laura

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:04:33 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Aurora AI competitive trial scope & bake-off success criteria

Got it — I’ll stand up the test harness in our staging cluster. Quick notes:
- We can expose KV cache hit/miss and per-request memory counters from the runtime; I’ll add those to the telemetry dashboard.
- For the stress stage, we’ll ramp in 10-second steps to 150 qps and keep each step for 2 minutes to observe tails.
- Need from Aurora: one representative 100-conversation sample for the summarization suite and the exact tokenization constraints you apply in prod (padding/truncation policy).

I’ll post the runbook link in Slack and attach a lightweight script for local smoke runs.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai | ext 2241

From: Priya Nambiar <priya@aurora.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:05:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Aurora AI competitive trial scope & bake-off success criteria

Thanks — we’re aligned. Sanjay and I signed the NDA this morning (attached NDA-signed.pdf).

We’ll:
- Drop sample prompts and one 100-conversation anonymized pack by EOD Monday (Aug 24) into the Drive link you provided.
- Confirm competitor endpoints (CloudGiant & HyperScale ML) and provide auth tokens for the test window by Aug 28.
- Smoke test: week of Aug 31 — we prefer Monday 9am PT if that slot works for you.

One ask re: deliverables — can you include an appendix in the final exec summary that lists the exact model variant/config used for each baseline (including quantization/precision settings)? That will help our infra team reconcile performance deltas.

Priya Nambiar
Director, Product Ops | Aurora AI
priya@aurora.ai | +1 (415) 555-0188

Attachments: NDA-signed.pdf
